summary: The main article describes a visible-light-mediated Minisci C-H alkylation of heteroarenes using unactivated alkyl halides and O2 as an oxidant. The document includes optimization tables, substrate scope tables for alkyl halides and heteroarenes, and mechanistic schemes including radical clock experiments.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Photoredox-mediated Minisci C -H alkylation of Nheteroarenes.
items.description: Compares previous Minisci alkylation methods using carboxylic acids or gold catalysts with the current work using alkyl halides and TTMS.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of conditions for alkylation of lepidine with bromocyclohexane a
items.description: Shows the screening of photocatalysts and solvents to optimize the yield of the alkylation reaction.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate scope with respect to alkyl halides a
items.description: Lists various primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl bromides and iodides used to functionalize lepidine.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Scope of the reaction with respect to the N-heteroarene a
items.description: Demonstrates the reaction scope across different nitrogen-containing heterocycles like quinolines, pyridines, and phenanthrolines.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Use of Minisci C -H alkylation for functionalization of natural products and drug molecules a
items.description: Shows the late-stage functionalization of complex molecules like quinine, fasudil, and loratadine.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Mechanistic experiments.
items.description: Details radical trapping and radical clock experiments used to support the proposed radical mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Proposed mechanism for direct C -H alkylation of heteroarenes.
items.description: Illustrates the catalytic cycle involving silyl radical generation, halogen abstraction, and oxidation by O2.
